proposal:
STATUS. Nothing was executed. Every number below is a hand derivation from the supplied code and needs independent re-checking. No polynomial-SAT claim.

A. MECHANISM: one-uphill DP excursion (OU-DP). The pinned elim accepts an elimination only if the canonical clause count does not rise. On the Neon58 quotient (48 clauses) every variable has 4 positive and 8 negative occurrences, so every first step gives 68 clauses and elim is STUCK. Yet only that first step is uphill. Rule: when elim is STUCK on F with c0 clauses, eliminate the variable minimising the post-canon count (ties: smallest id), provided the count is at most B = c0(1+ceil(log2 c0)). Then take greedy min-count steps, each strictly decreasing, for at most L steps. Commit once the count is <= c0; otherwise roll back to F and continue pinned v5 unchanged.
Hand trace on the quotient: counts 48, 68, 60, 56, 40 (commit), 36, 28, 24, 20, 19, 11, 10, 6, 5, empty clause. Elimination order: 1, 9, 3, 11, 5, 13, 7, 15, 2, 10, 4, 12, 6, 14. This is the pairing of the trusted peak-2 branch order, found from counts alone. Rejected alternatives at the second step: variable 3 gives 76, variable 2 gives 137. Independent-prototype prediction: UNSAT, zero branching, zero IALH calls.
For the k-pair family: start 2^(k+1)+k^2; after pair j the count is 2^k + k(k-j) + k*2^(k-j). There is one uphill step of ratio about (k+3)/4, logarithmic in input size, and recovery after about log2 k pairs.

B. SOUND RULE VERSUS UNPROVED BOUND. Soundness needs nothing new. Each step is exact existential projection, the lemma elim already relies on, with models rebuilt by the existing stack; rollback restores F. The certificate is the eliminated-variable list, checked by replay. Cost with the prefilter pos*neg <= B: each attempt makes at most B resolvents of width at most n, and naive subsumption costs O(B^2 n) literal comparisons. With n candidates and at most n steps this is O(n^3 B^2 log n) bit operations per excursion, one excursion per STUCK node. That bounds the excursion only. After a rollback, residual work is whatever v5 does.

C. WHAT IALH DOES ON NEON58 (audit). Restrict the quotient by 1=0, 2=0, 3=1, 4=1; the result is the 17-clause fixture. Every single elimination raises its count, so elim is STUCK. But window {5,6,9,13,14}, the union of supports {6,9,14} and {5,6,13,14}, has an empty UP table: all 32 cubes propagate to a conflict. So v5 refutes this state by five-variable cube lookahead, not lattice arithmetic. A model ignoring IALH finds nine elim-stuck states at layer 4, against the measured peak 8.

D. TOTAL WORK ON PIGEONHOLE (audit of windows/refute). Assumed encoding: one clause per pigeon, pairwise clauses per hole. For 5 pigeons into 4 holes I count 45 supports plus 40+20+600+80 unions = 785 windows. The cap of 256 keeps 40 pairs, 40 triples and 176 four-sets: 3296 tuples and no five-window. For 6 into 5: 2506 windows; kept 75+100+81, 2396 tuples; the six width-5 pigeon clauses are never tabled. Every kept table spans the full integer lattice. Hole windows contain the origin and all its single-flip neighbours; a pigeon four-window keeps exactly the weight-1 and weight-2 tuples. So hull_rows returns nothing. Predicted root_counting in both cases: windows=256, constraints=0, truncated=true. IALH is pure overhead there. In general, b binary clauses create on the order of b^2 four-windows that sort ahead of every five-window.
Two output-preserving repairs: STAR-SKIP (if a table contains a point and all its single-flip neighbours, skip hull_rows, since no row can exist and the table is non-empty) and a canonical-key memo for refute.

E. CERTIFICATE AUDIT. verify_certificate builds blocks from every original clause. It checks that used forms lie inside the block support, compares full local tables, and checks every entry of P*L=I. Hence F = Q after L with L onto, which gives equisatisfiability. The subset gate in probe is independent, and a quotient-stage UNSAT lifts through that equivalence. I found no soundness defect in the supplied text. Operational hazards only: recursive SCC depth, the lru key on non-canonical tuples, prune quadratic in pre-prune children, and SymPy HNF with no bit bound.
missing_theorem:
MT1 (restricted; elementary). For the k-pair family under any numbering, OU-DP with L >= 2*ceil(log2 k)+2 commits, and continued min-count elimination derives the empty clause with the counts in A. Replay-checkable in Lean for k <= 5.

MT2 (extras tolerance; conjecture). e extra clauses containing one module literal add e*2^(k-1) resolvents at the uphill step, and about e*k*2^(k-2) before B_j subsumes them. Conjecture: OU-DP commits while that stays below B - c0, which is only about 8 extras per module variable at the default cap. This needs a proof and a matching failing example.

MT3 (the real gap). Call F (L,rho)-recoverable if some elimination sequence of length at most L keeps counts at most rho*c0 and ends at most c0. Needed: greedy min-count finds a recovering sequence whenever one with comparable parameters exists. I expect this to be FALSE in general. Exhaustive search costs n^L, quasi-polynomial only when L = O(log log m).

MT4 (obstruction; cited from memory). OU-DP alone cannot be general. A committed chain with counts at most B is a resolution refutation of size at most n*B^2, so by Haken's pigeonhole lower bound every elimination order on pigeonhole has a superpolynomial intermediate formula. A general bound needs a non-resolution component with its own work bound. By D, the current lattice rows contribute nothing on pigeonhole.
self_attack:
1. Bounded-growth variable elimination is standard preprocessing (NiVER, SatELite, later growth bounds; cited from memory). Only the rollback excursion and its cost accounting are added.
2. The pair family never needed exponential work in encoded size. The gain is practical, not a complexity separation.
3. The trace arithmetic (68, 60, 56, 40; alternatives 76, 137, 52) is by hand. One missed subsumption or tie changes it.
4. Greedy min-count costs n attempts per step. Where no excursion commits it is pure overhead, the same disease as IALH on pigeonhole. It needs a trigger, for example root only.
5. C shows last round's certificate-free model of v5 was incomplete: empty-table lookahead matters. I have not simulated which layer-4 states survive.
6. D depends on my assumed pigeonhole encoding. STAR-SKIP saves HNF calls but not the 2^5 UP runs per window, which may dominate. Unmeasured.
7. The fixture is refuted by existing code. It tests audit claim C, not OU-DP.
8. Arbitrary extras are tolerated only up to a constant per module variable. Incompatible GF(2) spaces, nested modules needing two uphills, and random 3-CNF are untouched.
mechanism_signature: One-uphill DP excursion with rollback (greedy min-count, cap c0(1+log2 c0)); excursion-recoverability as the work invariant; IALH identified as five-cube UP lookahead; window-starvation counts and star-skip.
delta_from_prior: Rounds 104-105 and Fable73 contracted twins with new certificates; round 106 changed branch order. This round uses neither. It projects a module by resolution with one bounded uphill step, reusing existing DP soundness. New audit facts: an explicit empty-table window on a Neon58 state, pigeonhole window counts 785 and 2506 with zero rows, and the resolution obstruction MT4. Independent test for the unimplemented part: an OU-DP prototype on the Neon58 quotient should reproduce the count sequence in A exactly. The fixture should also give baseline peak at least 1 (no IALH) and a root certificate of kind empty_table.
